newsitem.title: UK: UK Minister Hogg plans to clear cow cull backlog.
newsitem.headline: UK Minister Hogg plans to clear cow cull backlog.

text.p: British Agriculture Douglas Hogg on Tuesday announced plans to tackle the backlog of cows being slaughtered under its scheme to stamp out mad cow disease.
Farmers will also be given a 29 million pound ($45.36 million) package of financial support, he told BBC Radio.
Hogg conceded that the chances of getting the European Union lifting its ban on British beef in the short-term was slim.
"It is certainly not going to be lifted completely and immediately. That is absolutely the case," he said.
Hogg said he intends to increase the weekly cull level to 55,000 from its present average of 23,000. The backlog should be cleared by Christmas, he added.
"The backlog under the cull scheme is very much larger than we expected. There is scope for real concern there," he said.

Traditionally pro-Conservative farmers are angry at plans to slaughter thousands of their cattle to stamp out Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) following scientific evidence that it may be transmissable to humans.
Some believe Hogg's negotiating tactics in Brussels to try to lift the ban and the government's handling of the technical aspects of the cull have made a bad situation even worse.
Hogg told BBC Radio: "The disease is dying out and will die out by around 2001 or thereabouts."
